articles.t: UK hacker who leaked GTA 6 footage years before release jailed for 7 years
articles.chapeau: Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty last week to hacking major companies between 2021 and 2022, including GTA-maker Rockstar Games and ride-hailing giant Uber
articles.txt:
A UK court sentenced a British hacker to seven years in jail Monday for a series of cyberattacks, including leaking footage from Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 , years before the blockbuster game's release.
Having already served years in custody, Arion Kurtaj, aged 21, was entitled to walk free immediately, Judge Mark Turner said at London's Woolwich Crown Court.
Kurtaj, who is autistic, pleaded guilty last week to hacking major companies between 2021 and 2022, including GTA-maker Rockstar Games, mobile operator BT/EE, digital bank Revolut and ride-hailing giant Uber.
Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.
Turner described the offences as "sophisticated attacks upon big companies".
The judge said his sentencing decision required "balancing the seriousness of what you did with, on the other hand, your young age" and medical diagnoses.
Kurtaj was a teenager when he carried out the attacks as a key member of the so-called Lapsus$ hacking group.
He was initially charged over hacking BT/EE and placed in a hotel for his own protection from rival hackers in September 2022, according to the Crown Prosecution Service.
But from his hotel room, he went on to carry out cyberattacks on Revolut, Uber and Rockstar.
Using just a mobile phone, the hotel's wifi-connected TV and an Amazon Fire TV Stick, he broke into Rockstar systems and obtained 90 videos of the highly-anticipated GTA VI game.
He leaked the videos online under the username "TeaPotUberHacker," more than a year before the first official footage was released by Rockstar, causing a frenzy across the video game industry.
The hack disrupted the release strategy for the sixth installment of the GTA franchise, which was finally released last week after a 13-year wait.
In 2023, a jury concluded that Kurtaj, whom psychiatrists at the time had deemed unfit to stand trial, was responsible for numerous computer misuse, fraud and blackmail offences.
Due to the severity of his autism, he was placed under a hospital order where he remained for two years before being found fit to stand trial, his lawyers said.

articles.t: GTA 6’s Best-Kept Secret Is the Key to Its Whole Design
articles.chapeau: It all begins and ends with one very specific character.
articles.txt: Warning: this story contains spoilers for GTA 6’s prologue and Chapter 1. In the final months of trailers, screenshots, and extended looks leading up to Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s launch, Rockstar was keeping a huge secret. It had revealed Jason and Lucia to the world years before and, by the summer of this year, we knew that their romantic relationship was core to the story. But until the moment the game went live, we had no idea that the pair were parents. As we all found out in the prologue, Jason and Lucia have a son, Tomás. And more than just a baby, this little infant is the key to GTA 6’s entire design ethos. Historically, Rockstar has drawn from classic crime movie tropes to establish the themes of its stories. Tommy Vercetti cut through all in his path on his way to becoming Miami’s premier crime lord. Carl Johnson rallied the boys in the hood on his quest for revenge. And Niko Bellic put his war-honed killing skills to work on the streets of Liberty City. While there are elements of relatability in all these stories – hurt over dead mothers, discovering the lie of the American dream – you’d be in the tiny minority of players if you could claim to truly recognise the lives of GTA’s protagonists as reflections of your own timeline.

Patrick has also interviewed dozens of tech industry executives and covered GDC, E3, Gamescom, WWDC, Apple keynotes, Samsung Unpacked events and more. Patrick has a BA in journalism from Toronto Metropolitan University. Sign in to your XDA account Summary Cyberleek has publicly released the missing GTA 6 Xbox executable. Unofficial PC port efforts like Leonida, an AI-assisted, static recompilation, are translating shaders to run the Xbox build on PC. Rockstar hasn't announced an official GTA 6 PC release; fan ports or emulation could produce a playable PC build soon. Cyberleek, the same individual or group behind the GTA 6 leaks from earlier this year, said they planned to release the missing Xbox executable for Grand Theft Auto 6 ( GTA 6 ) , and they've followed through. The file is now publicly available, completing the 209GB Xbox build Cyberleek leaked last week on private torrent trackers.
On their website, Cyberleek wrote that "the exe is out. Always free." Cyberleek also published SHA-256 hashes for GTA 6's executable and its ZIP archive, emphasizing that users should verify the files before downloading them. Cyberleek's website appears to be down right now. Several GTA 6 PC porting projects are underway, but the most notable is Leonida, from the same developer behind one of the best early PC static recompilations of the Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time .
Leonida aims to bring the Xbox version of GTA 6 to Windows through a static recompilation that includes shader translation and an Xbox compatibility runtime. Because Xbox Series X/S consoles and Windows PCs share the x86-64 CPU architecture, the project can potentially run a lot of the game's CPU code natively.
NotRexed , the Leonida's developer, says that all 26,503 RDNA2 shaders have already been translated to Vulkan SPIR-V. The other compatibility tools that are needed to run the Xbox version of GTA 6 on PC are also in the works, according to NotRexed. Of course, like nearly every similar project that's launched recently, Lenoida is AI-assisted.
Credit: Rockstar While the Xbox build of GTA 6 leaked last week, it was missing its executable, which kept developers eager to port the game to PC from truly starting their projects. So what does this all mean?
Well, a playable PC version of GTA 6 could launch in the next few days if projects like Leonida can pull off the porting process. Alongside Leonida, there are broader Xbox Series X/S translation and emulation efforts like Xbox2Windows , ScarlettX , and AnyXboxX .
In other GTA 6 -related news, with PS5 Remote Play or a capture card, plus apps like Veyra and a powerful gaming PC, several people have been able to run GTA 6 at 60fps and above with DLSS 5 . While GTA 6 is now available on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, Rockstar hasn't announced a PC version. Rumors point to an official PC release arriving somewhere between six months and a year from now, similar to GTA V .

articles.txt:
The hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak in September 2022 has been released on license with a strong warning from the judge. Having already served the majority of his seven year sentence, Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford in the United Kingdom, was allowed to go free, conditionally.
According to the BBC , the judge warned Kurtaj: "Don't let this happen again."
Kurtaj attempted to extort GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games in 2022. After socially engineering his way into the company Slack, the now 21-year-old threatened to release clips of the unfinished game unless Rockstar paid a ransom. He pleaded guilty to the hacking offenses , which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old, earlier this week.
⚖️ Arion Kurtaj, 21, has been convicted today for targeting major international companies, hacking into their private systems, stealing information and data, and causing millions of dollars in losses. 📰 https://t.co/UvJTCFWnct https://t.co/3CoLIw7dDs
Originally, Kurtaj was sentenced to an indefinite stay in a prison hospital due to his autism diagnosis. After reconsideration, he was deemed fit to stand trial and spent the remainder of his time in a traditional prison, starting in January.
With his release, Kurtaj has been given a Serious Crime Prevention Order, which restricts his interactions online, barring him from using social apps like Telegram and Discord, in an attempt to prevent him working with hacker groups. The order will last for five years.
The hack happened while Kurtaj was already under police protection in a Travelodge with his computer confiscated. During his stay, he used an Amazon Fire Stick and the hotel television to hack Rockstar, Revolut, and Uber.
The GTA 6 hack saw him steal 90 clips of an unfinished build well before Rockstar was ready to show gameplay from its anticipated open-world sequel, which launched last week. It resulted in the first major GTA 6 leak, as early gameplay footage was shared online. Here, we saw dual protagonists Jason and Lucia for the first time. These clips were shared under the online name TeaPotUberHacker. It would be over a year before Rockstar finally showed the protagonists itself, and even longer until we got an official gameplay reveal, which was only shared in August of this year.
"If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code," he said in the company Slack. When the company didn’t respond, he released the files, costing the company $5 million in damages.

articles.chapeau: CYBERLEEK made good on their promise, posting the executable of the previously leaked Xbox Series build of Grand Theft Auto VI.
articles.txt:
CYBERLEEK , the anonymous hacker/leaker (or group) responsible for the major pre-release Grand Theft Auto VI footage leaks, has now delivered on their final promise: posting the Xbox build's executable after already sharing the rest of the files, as an "early Christmas gift".
The document published alongside the release, available on Pastebin , says:
CYBERLEEK is about fighting anti-consumerism in the games industry. It was never about damaging the players. The players have no fault in any of this. That is why the ending was never leaked, and why the story mode was never spoiled. Millions waited years for this game, and ruining that experience would mean hurting exactly the people CYBERLEEK stands with. The enemy is the tactic, not the game: subscriptions bolted onto single-player games, 20-dollar "ultimate editions" that unlock what already sits in the game files, licenses sold as purchases. All of it needs to be eliminated.
"Untouchable" is supposed to be a word for billion dollar companies. This release says otherwise. Months of takedowns, subpoenas and wallet tracing later, the hunt is still on and the uploads keep arriving. No budget makes a lock unbreakable, and no court order deletes what the internet already has. The rules hold only as long as people obey them. This Grand Theft Auto VI build is what it looks like when someone does not.
What really matters for PC gamers, though, is that this could be the gateway to a playable build ahead of the official release. NotRexed , the same modder behind Hookshot (the native PC recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake ), was waiting just for the executable to go ahead with the Leonida project, a static recompilation project to get the Xbox Series version running on PC:
The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens on your PC, from your own copy of the game .
Early. The game does not boot yet. Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer.
It should be noted that NotRexed had previously recompiled The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom , but that repository is nowhere to be found, likely because Nintendo nuked it. The same might very well befall the equivalent Grand Theft Auto VI project.
Still, the clock is ticking. We might get at least a demonstration of Rockstar's new masterpiece running natively on PC relatively soon. Meanwhile, the game continues to sell gangbusters on consoles , and Rockstar also just dropped The Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album (Deluxe Edition) .

Smallest Font Largest Font A reported leak of Grand Theft Auto 6's Xbox development build has prompted Cyberleek to claim that modders could make the game playable on PC within a week. The claim, reported by TweakTown on November 22, 2026, comes despite missing essential files and Rockstar Games ' warning of potential legal action against unauthorized PC versions. The leaked files reportedly contain a nearly complete Xbox build of GTA 6 .
However, the game's main executable is missing, alongside several other system files that could prevent the software from running properly on Windows computers. According to TweakTown, no independent demonstration has confirmed that the leaked build can operate as a complete PC game. Consequently, the proposed one-week development timeline remains an unverified claim rather than a demonstrated technical achievement.
One factor potentially simplifying the conversion process is the Xbox Gaming Development Kit (GDK) architecture. Unlike traditional console software that may require extensive hardware-specific modifications, the reported build shares significant architectural similarities with Windows.
Modder OptiJuegos highlighted this compatibility, explaining that the existing architecture could reduce the technical work required to adapt the Xbox version for Windows. This could eliminate the need to translate certain console-specific hardware instructions from scratch. Nevertheless, the missing executable remains a substantial obstacle. The additional absent system files have also not been specifically identified, leaving uncertainty about whether modders can overcome the remaining technical limitations.
VX Underground has also provided information concerning the authenticity of the leaked material. The group said it examined the Xbox files and discovered game assets, leading it to believe the leak was genuine. However, identifying authentic game assets does not establish that the leaked package contains everything necessary to launch GTA 6. VX Underground's findings do not independently demonstrate that the files can run as a complete Windows application.
Rockstar Games has previously indicated that it would take unauthorized attempts to bring GTA 6 to PC seriously. The company has warned that it could pursue legal action against individuals attempting illegal ports or unauthorized AI-generated copies of the game. The potential legal consequences add another complication for modders considering an unofficial Windows release.
Rockstar's position makes clear that technical progress alone would not eliminate the legal risks associated with distributing an unauthorized version. Meanwhile, Rockstar has not officially announced a PC release date for GTA 6. An early 2027 launch has been anticipated, although the company has not confirmed that timeframe.
Separate reports have suggested that Rockstar could accelerate its official PC port following recent breakthroughs in game emulation and recompilation. However, no confirmed release schedule or revised launch plan has been announced.

articles.txt:
Suivez LEBIGDATA.FR G o o g l e News Discover Ajouter comme source préférée Relu par Bastien L. , Rédacteur en chef
Attendre la sortie de GTA 6 le 19 novembre était déjà pénible. Alors, espérer l’arrivée d’une éventuelle version PC que Rockstar n’a pas encore annoncée, je ne vous le fais pas dire.
Mais depuis quelques jours, les joueurs PC sont enthousiastes. Pourquoi ? Parce qu’une communauté de pirates travaille à adapter une version Xbox du jeu aux ordinateurs.
Le groupe en question est connu sous le nom de Cyberleek. Oui, le même groupe qui a diffusé des images de GTA 6 et menacé de diffuser le jeu avant sa sortie officielle .
Le 19 novembre 2026, Cyberleek a diffusé une archive de 209 Go présentée comme une version Xbox Series X|S de GTA 6.
Celle-ci contient notamment des textures, des modèles 3D, des effets sonores et des shaders. Ces derniers sont des programmes qui participent au rendu graphique du jeu.
En clair, une bonne partie des éléments nécessaires à la représentation de l’univers de GTA 6 serait déjà disponible. Mais il manque une pièce essentielle au puzzle : l’exécutable principal .
Ce fichier contient les instructions permettant de lancer le programme. Sans lui, même avec des centaines de gigaoctets de ressources, impossible de démarrer une partie.
Cyberleek a annoncé vouloir publier ce fichier le 23 novembre . Toutefois, ses précédentes promesses non tenues obligent à prendre cette annonce avec des pincettes. Pour l’instant, rien ne permet d’affirmer qu’une version pirate fonctionnelle est disponible.
Le choix de la version Xbox n’est pas anodin. La Xbox Series X utilise une architecture x86-64 , que l’on retrouve également dans les processeurs de nombreux ordinateurs.
Cela facilite certaines opérations d’adaptation. Les développeurs n’ont pas besoin de repartir entièrement de zéro pour comprendre comment le jeu fonctionne.
Par ailleurs, un développeur connu sous le pseudonyme NotRexed entreprend de le faire avec son projet open source , baptisé Leonida , récemment apparu sur GitHub .
Bon, techniquement, il ne s’agit pas de recréer le jeu, mais de travailler à partir de ses ressources existantes. Le développeur cherche notamment à adapter les éléments graphiques et les composants logiciels nécessaires pour permettre au jeu de fonctionner dans un environnement PC.
Et les premiers résultats de Leonida sont déjà visibles. Le projet a notamment traduit 26 503 shaders vers Vulkan , une technologie qui permet de gérer l’affichage graphique sur différentes configurations matérielles.
Il permet aussi d’extraire des modèles 3D, des textures et des fichiers audio présents dans les données récupérées. L’intelligence artificielle participe également à ce travail.
Des agents de programmation assistent certaines opérations, ce qui peut accélérer le traitement de nombreux fichiers. Mais même avec cette aide, adapter un jeu aussi complexe n’est pas une mince affaire.

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : une version pirate dès aujourd'hui ?
articles.chapeau: Quatre jours après la publication d'une build Xbox de GTA 6 par Cyberleek, un projet open source baptisé Leonida affirme avoir préparé tout ce qu'il faut pour faire tourner le jeu sur PC. Le seul problème est qu'il manque toujours le fichier qui lance le jeu. Certains affirment qu'il pourrait être publié dès le 23
articles.txt:
Recevez tous les soirs un résumé de l’actu importante avec Le Récap’
Si vous vous intéressez à l’émulation, vous avez forcément entendu parler du projet Leonida. Ce dépôt GitHub promet de transformer la version Xbox Series X de GTA 6 en un jeu PC natif et beaucoup de comptes sur les réseaux sociaux le présentent comme un portage quasiment terminé. Le développeur, qui s’est aidé de l’IA pour tout coder en seulement quelques heures, est convaincu que son logiciel permettra à des millions de joueurs PC de découvrir GTA 6 au moment où l’exécutable du jeu sera publié. Mais est-ce vraiment plausible ?
Le projet est sérieux, mais il ne peut pas démarrer le jeu. Cyberleek affirme qu’il va publier les fichiers manquants le 23 novembre, mais tout miser sur un compte qui veut faire fructifier sa cryptomonnaie est un pari osé. Beaucoup de fausses vidéos circulent sur les réseaux sociaux.
GTA 6 sur PC : entre la build Cyberleek et les extractions PS5, la pression s’accentue pour Rockstar GTA 6 pour Xbox a fuité, mais il est impossible de démarrer le jeu Le 19 novembre, jour de la sortie de GTA 6 , Cyberleek a mis en ligne par torrent une archive de 209 Go présentée comme la build Xbox 1.0.2.1 du jeu, datée de novembre 2026. Le jeu est a priori authentique, mais il n’est pas jouable. L’exécutable principal, celui qui lance le jeu et qui contient tout son code, n’a pas été publié par Cyberleek.
Sans lui, l’archive n’est qu’un immense stock de modèles 3D, de textures, de sons et de shaders. Certains s’amusent à extraire la carte ou les voitures, mais la build est injouable.
Black Friday : Proton Pass Plus à -60 % Jusqu’au 30 novembre, Proton Pass Plus est à 1,99 € par mois pendant 12 mois, soit 60 % de réduction ! Alias d’adresse mail illimités pour profiter des codes promo sans saturer votre boîte, mot de passe unique par site, coffre-fort chiffré. Bref, un Black Friday sans stress ! Sponsorisé En ce moment à 1,99€ par mois Leonida sur Github. // Source : Capture Numerama Le leaker Cyberleek, déjà à l’origine de fuites massives cet été, tient le même discours depuis jeudi : l’exécutable sortira ce lundi 23 novembre « sans condition » (ou plus tôt si son memecoin $CYBERLEEK atteint une certaine capitalisation). Le pirate promet aussi que la communauté pourra émuler le jeu « en une semaine », Et si la build Xbox ne suffit pas, il assure qu’il cherchera à obtenir une build PS5. Bref, Cyberleek veut nuire à Rockstar. Cyberleek, qui se fait passer pour un « pirate militant » , est une personnalité très controversée. Tout suggère que ses motivations sont surtout financières et qu’il ne faut pas lui faire confiance.
Rappel important : si l’émulation en tant que telle n’est pas illégale dans tous les pays, elle nécessite toujours d’utiliser sa propre copie du jeu. Ce que propose Cyberleek est illégal et utiliser une build provenant d’un leaker aux objectifs malveillants n’est pas une bonne idée. Take-Two va probablement tout faire pour combattre le projet et est dans son droit.
En attendant des nouvelles de Cyberleek, la sphère de l’émulation PC s’active. Le projet Leonida est apparu sur GitHub le 20 novembre. Son créateur, NotRexed, n’est pas un inconnu : il est l’un des développeurs de Hookshot, le projet qui a porté sur PC le remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time sorti sur Switch 2 à peine un jour après sa sortie.
Le principe s’appelle la recompilation statique. Le processeur de la Xbox Series utilise la même architecture x86-64 qu’un PC : le code du jeu peut donc tourner tel quel, sans émulation, à condition de recréer autour de lui tout ce que la console lui fournit (son système, ses bibliothèques Microsoft, sa version de DirectX). Les shaders, ces petits programmes graphiques compilés pour la puce AMD de la console, doivent eux être traduits pour Vulkan.
Le projet revendique déjà la traduction des 26 503 shaders du jeu, l’export des modèles, des textures et des banques audio, un chargeur capable de lancer un exécutable de test et une couche graphique qui commence à dessiner sur Vulkan. Le rythme est sans précédent : plus de 8 600 modifications en trois jours, des dizaines de contributeurs et plus de 17 000 étoiles sur GitHub. Le projet ne cache pas son recours massif à l’IA : il a des consignes dédiées aux agents de code et demande de signaler toute contribution assistée.

articles.t: « Tournant bien au-delà des 30 fps » GTA 6 pourrait débarquer sur PC bien avant sa sortie officielle. Un hacker menace Rockstar
articles.chapeau: Alors que GTA 6 vient de sortir sur consoles, le leaker ou groupe de leakers Cyberleek refait surface. Cette fois, il menace Rockstar de sortir une version du jeu jouable sur PC.
articles.txt:
Alors que GTA 6 vient de sortir sur consoles, le leaker ou groupe de leakers Cyberleek refait surface. Cette fois, il menace Rockstar de sortir une version du jeu jouable sur PC.
Et si GTA 6 débarquait sur PC de manière complètement illégale ? C'est en tout cas la promesse de Cyberleek, le leaker ou groupe de leakers qui partageait des extraits de gameplay du jeu avant sa sortie. Mais maintenant que ce dernier est disponible sur PS5 et XBOX Series X|S, il prévient Rockstar qu'il est sur le point de passer aux choses sérieuses en menaçant de sortir une version tournant à plus de 30 FPS en émulation.
Il est de retour et ça risque de ne pas plaire à Rockstar. Après avoir diffusé en ligne des extraits vidéos du gameplay de GTA 6 avant la sortie du jeu, Cyberleek pourrait maintenant aller beaucoup plus loin. Jusqu'ici, le leaker avait vraisemblablement en sa possession une build du jeu datant de plusieurs années. Or, il aurait à présent une build quasi-complète d'une version Xbox.
C'est en tout cas ce que le leaker annonce sur son site Internet. Mais bien sûr, il ne se contente pas de préciser cela. Il promet surtout que « la communauté aura accès à une version émulée tournant bien au-delà des 30 fps d'ici à une semaine ». Cela veut dire que Cyberleek est prêt à partager l'exécutable de GTA 6 sur PC.
Le message remonte au 19 novembre et annonce également que Cyberleek travaille à récupérer une version PS5. Mais d'ici-là, le leaker demande à recevoir 15 millions de market cap dollars (sa crypto monnaie) pour sortir l'exécutable de la version Xbox sur PC. Le fichier est déjà annoncé comme pesant plus de 200 Go , ce qui est cohérent avec le poids du jeu sur console.
Avec cette menace, Cyberleek tente donc de couper l'herbe sous le pied de Rockstar Games et Take-Two Interactive. En effet, GTA 6 n'a pas encore de date de sortie annoncée sur PC et cela frustre assurément une partie de la communauté. Il n'en faut alors pas plus pour que le leaker s'enfonce dans la brèche et tente d'en tirer profit. Il vise même toutes celles et ceux qui recherche les performances avec cette idée que sa version pourrait potentiellement atteindre les 60 fps inatteignables sur consoles. Attention alors à la sortie de cette version hackée qui pourrait bien arriver dès aujourd'hui sur la toile.

articles.t: Developers Pursue GTA 6 PC Port From Leaked Xbox Build
articles.chapeau: Three GitHub projects are exploring an unofficial GTA 6 PC port using a leaked 209 GB Xbox build, but the main executable remains missing.
articles.txt:
120 Reads Last Update Nov 23, 2026 - 14:32 Share WhatsApp Jason and Lucia robbing a bank vault in GTA 6 Smallest Font Largest Font Three community development teams are investigating ways to run Grand Theft Auto VI on Windows PCs using a leaked 209 GB Xbox Series X|S package. The files, attributed to leaker Cyberleek, have circulated on torrent networks since the game's November 19 launch, but developers cannot boot the game because its main executable is missing.
The projects, Leonida, Xbox2Windows, and AnyXboxX, are examining the game's code and graphics resources to develop unofficial compatibility solutions. None has demonstrated a working launch of GTA VI so far.
Cyberleek claims the package contains version 1.0.2.1 of a November 2026 build. According to a statement reported by PC Gamer, the leaker plans to release the missing executable on November 23, regardless of market conditions, or earlier if the CYBERLEEK memecoin reaches a $15 million market capitalization.
That target represents half the $30 million objective the token failed to achieve in October. PC Gamer, citing Cyberleek's website, reported that the cryptocurrency was valued at approximately $1.83 million when the statement appeared.
Cyberleek also made a prediction about the project's potential progress:
"This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps." Cyberleek said.
However, neither the authenticity of the leaked package nor the claims about its contents have been independently verified. Rockstar has not confirmed that the files represent an authentic Xbox build of GTA VI.
One development project has also identified signature hash mismatches in 12 DLL files, according to its findings. The team has not established why those discrepancies exist, while earlier fake builds associated with Cyberleek's name were found to contain malware.
Leonida has made progress by exploiting the similarities between Xbox and PC processors. The Xbox Series X|S uses an AMD Zen 2 CPU with an x86-64 instruction set, allowing the project to execute the game's processor code natively rather than translating it.
This differs from projects such as Liberty Recompiled, which brings the Xbox 360 version of GTA IV to PC and must first convert the console's PowerPC instructions into C++.
Graphics compatibility remains a separate challenge. Leonida says it has translated all 26,503 RDNA 2 shaders into SPIR-V, the format used by Vulkan, and that every shader passes the format's structural validation.
However, passing validation does not establish that the shaders produce correct visual results. The project also faces compatibility issues involving 21,545 wave64 programs designed for AMD's 64-wide processing groups, compared with the 32-wide execution groups used by Nvidia and Intel GPUs.
Leonida says its emulation of wider processing groups is exact for compute and mesh shaders but remains approximate for certain vertex, pixel, and geometry shader operations.
Xbox2Windows follows a different approach, translating selected x64 instructions into C++ and converting shaders into DXIL, the format used by DirectX 12. Its documentation identifies the missing executable as the main obstacle.
The project has compiled 851 of GTA VI's 12,101 pixel shaders so far, with those shaders matching controlled test outputs, according to its development notes.
AnyXboxX, a prototype Xbox Series X emulator, can execute code directly on the host processor or through the Unicorn CPU emulator in an isolated environment. Its package inventory identified 103 of the 104 expected files, with the main executable accounting for the missing item.
Its current shader research covers a Microsoft ray-tracing library included with the game rather than GTA VI's own shaders. Research notes also indicate that the game's mesh shaders lack root signatures, which map shaders to their required resources, with those structures reportedly contained in the missing executable.
November 23 represents the next milestone for the three projects if Cyberleek delivers the promised file. Even with access to the executable, successfully launching GTA VI and achieving playable frame rates would remain separate technical challenges.
